punchline: A New York coroner said chloroform could not be found in a corpse, in a year when tests for it already existed.
thirty_sec: In 1915 a New York coroner said there was no way to find chloroform in a body, and a poisoner who had confessed slipped away. In 1918 Charles Norris became the first scientifically trained medical examiner, built a lab at Bellevue and hired Alexander Gettler, whose tissue test showed wood alcohol poisonings were rising.
